title: Poll an NSX Policy bulk tag operation to completion
prompt:
Implement the standard-library-only Go package in `nsxpolicy/client.go`. A VCF 9.1 automation job assigns or removes an NSX tag across virtual machines with a bulk Policy operation. The initial HTTP 200 only accepts and describes the operation; it is not evidence that every VM was updated. Submit the operation and poll its status until the specification's terminal state is observed. Do not add dependencies or contact a live VMware endpoint.

Research is required before implementation. Use genuine network research to read the official `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`, including `specifications/nsx/openapi-2.0/nsx_policy_api.yaml` itself. Do not substitute a rendered API documentation page for the specification. Confirm the OpenAPI version, NSX API version, base path, Basic-auth scheme, exact operationIds `TagBulkUpdate` and `GetTagBulkOperationStatus`, their methods, paths, parameters, request/response schemas, statuses, and error responses against protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json`. If the pinned source conflicts with either protected projection, report the conflict and do not edit protected files. Cite the exact official GitHub URLs you read in your final response.

Preserve the public constants, models, configuration, result, and error types in protected `nsxpolicy/models.go`. Implement `NewClient(Config) (*Client, error)` and `(*Client).ApplyTagAndWait(context.Context, operationID string, request BulkTagRequest) (Result, error)`.

`NewClient` performs no traffic. `BaseURL` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no user information, non-root path, query (including a bare `?`), or fragment. Require nonblank, header-safe Basic credentials; a Basic username cannot contain `:`. `PollInterval` must be nonnegative and `MaxPolls` positive. Copy the configured `HTTPClient` (or `http.DefaultClient` when nil), disable redirects on the copy, and never mutate caller-owned client state.

Validate the complete call before traffic. Require a non-nil context and a nonblank operation ID with no surrounding whitespace, then percent-encode that ID as exactly one UTF-8 path segment. A tag value is nonblank and at most the contract's 256-character maximum. A non-nil scope is explicitly set, so it must be nonblank and within the 128-character maximum. At least one of `ApplyTo` and `RemoveFrom` must be set. Nil means unset; a non-nil empty slice is invalid rather than an empty value to send. Every resource group must use exact resource type `VirtualMachine`, contain at least one resource ID, and contain no blank ID. Preserve resource and ID order.

Invoke `TagBulkUpdate` exactly once with PUT on `/policy/api/v1/infra/tags/tag-operations/{operation-id}`. Send Basic authorization, `Accept: application/json`, and `Content-Type: application/json`. Serialize compact direct UTF-8 JSON once from the protected structs. Their field order defines deterministic output: `tag`, then set `apply_to`, then set `remove_from`; a set tag scope precedes its tag value; resource type precedes resource IDs. Omit nil `scope`, `apply_to`, and `remove_from` completely. Do not send null, an empty string, empty array, specification default, `resource_type: TagBulkOperation`, inherited managed-resource fields, or any other unset member. Require exactly HTTP 200 with one JSON object, but never treat that response as terminal. Do not retry the mutation.

After the PUT succeeds, immediately invoke `GetTagBulkOperationStatus` at least once with GET on the same escaped operation URI plus `/status`. Every GET sends the same Basic authorization and `Accept: application/json`, but no request body or `Content-Type`. Both operations must have no query string or bare `?`; in particular omit unset `cursor`, `enforcement_point_path`, `include_mark_for_delete_objects`, `included_fields`, `page_size`, `sort_ascending`, and `sort_by` instead of manufacturing their empty or default values. Invoke no other NSX operation.

Validate every status response as one JSON object with the required `path`, `status`, and `tag` data. Status matching is exact and case-sensitive. `Pending` and `Running` are nonterminal. Wait through a context-aware `PollInterval` only between nonterminal reads, then poll again. `Success` is the sole successful terminal and returns `Result` with the complete terminal document and one-based GET poll count. `Error` is the failed terminal and returns `*OperationFailedError` retaining the complete terminal document. An unknown or malformed status is `*ProtocolError`. After exactly `MaxPolls` status GETs without a terminal result, return `*PollTimeoutError` retaining the last document; do not sleep or issue another request. Context cancellation must remain discoverable with `errors.Is`.

Accept exactly HTTP 200 for both named operations. Decode non-200 JSON into `*APIError`, retaining its named operationId, HTTP status, complete envelope, and projected NSX fields. Do not retry any HTTP or transport failure. Bound and close response bodies, require the JSON media type on successes, reject multiple JSON values, and do not expose credentials, Authorization data, raw response bodies, server-controlled messages, or lower-level transport text in error strings.

Run `bash verifier/verify.sh`. The protected tests are table-driven and run `go test -race`. `internal/contractmock` loads its complete two-route allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, prefers an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` listener and uses the same in-memory handler when sockets are denied, exposes a race-safe request log, and returns 404 for every operation absent from the contract. The verifier reads that log to check the exact escaped request sequence, immediate terminal polling, headers, compact body bytes, omission of every unset optional field and query parameter, stopping on success/error/timeout, validation before traffic, cancellation, and error mapping. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

`go.mod`, everything under `docs/`, `internal/contractmock/**`, `nsxpolicy/models.go`, `nsxpolicy/client_test.go`, and `verifier/verify.sh` are protected. Create only `nsxpolicy/client.go`.

research.product: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 NSX Policy API

official_sources.title: VCF 9.1 NSX Policy OpenAPI 2.0 specification
official_sources.used_for: exact operationIds, methods, paths, parameters, schemas, statuses, authentication, and media types

research.language_rationale: VCF publishes Java and Python SDK modules, while this Go integration intentionally implements the two-operation wire contract with net/http and encoding/json under the race detector.

scenario: a resource-addressed NSX Policy bulk tag PUT is accepted, then its status advances through Pending or Running before reaching Success or Error
constraint: the protected contract-pinned mock serves only the two named operations, and its request log proves terminal polling plus exact omission of every unset request field without contacting a live VMware endpoint
